Ellen —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short workbook (HealthGuard_capacity_workbook_v3.xlsx) and a draft mutual-action-plan (HG-MAP-draft.pdf). TL;DR: for a 3-month pilot targeting your stated P99 and midweek peak loads (baseline tests from your demo), we recommend two trial paths:

- Dedicated pilot (fastest time-to-demo): 8 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (2 nodes, 4 GPU each), continuous autoscale cap to +2 nodes for bursts. Expected token throughput to meet a 600ms P99 for your median prompt mix. Estimated committed monthly spend (incl. support & egress): $95k/mo.

- Private pilot (VPC, customer-controlled networking): 6 x A40-equivalent GPUs (single tenant image, better data isolation), with reserved capacity and a small burst pool (1 extra node). Higher setup/provisioning cadence and network approval needed. Estimated monthly TCO (ops + infra amortized): $140k/mo for pilot.

We included conservative headroom for KV caching inefficiencies and cold-cache penalty. The workbook has a sensitivity tab (latency by sequence length and batch size) and a procurement-ready line-item view.

Cutoffs for recommending Private over Dedicated (guidelines, not strict rules):
- If customer requires customer-managed key material (HSM/KMS inside their VPC) -> Private.
- Sustained 24x7 peak above 120 RPS for Gen-2 LLMs or >1.5B tokens/day (predictable heavy throughput) -> lean Private to avoid burst pricing surprises.
- Regulatory mandate for full network air-gapping, onsite logs retention, or on-prem -> Private.

Otherwise, Dedicated is usually the lower-risk quick path for first 6 months if compliance controls in our dedicated offering (VPC peering, audited logs, SOC attestation) are acceptable.

Proposed next steps in MAP:
1) Procurement review (HealthGuard) — confirm preferred path by Nov 9.
2) Finalize SOW and commit level for pilot within two weeks after procurement sign-off.
3) Technical kickoff and baseline latency test on your recorded prompt set.

I'll schedule a budget walkthrough with Karthik and Marissa.

Best,
Olga
